name: Trastuzumab emtansine (T-DM1)
drug_class: HER2-directed antibody linked to the microtubule inhibitor DM1
mechanism: HER2 binding delivers the linked DM1 payload into cells. DM1 acts on tubulin and disrupts cell division. This is one linked medicine with its own dose and toxicity rules; it is not interchangeable with trastuzumab alone or trastuzumab deruxtecan.
review_status: Source checked — independent clinical/pharmacy review pending

name: Tucatinib
mechanism: Inhibits HER2 kinase activity and downstream growth signalling. In this breast regimen it is combined with capecitabine and trastuzumab, with a continuous tablet schedule separate from the capecitabine break.
review_status: Source checked — independent clinical/pharmacy review pending

name: Ribociclib
mechanism: Blocks cyclin-dependent kinases 4 and 6, slowing cell-cycle progression. Used with endocrine treatment in selected HR-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer. Adjuvant and advanced-disease starting doses differ; use the indication-specific NCCP regimen.
review_status: Source checked — independent clinical/pharmacy review pending

name: Abemaciclib
mechanism: Blocks cyclin-dependent kinases 4 and 6, slowing cell-cycle progression. Its continuous dosing and monitoring plan differ from ribociclib. Use the specific breast indication and endocrine partner described in the NCCP regimen.
review_status: Source checked — independent clinical/pharmacy review pending
